intro.title: forwardRef & Exposing DOM Nodes
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that uses a button to focus on a text input field. You will learn how to use forwardRef to resolve circular dependencies when accessing a component's template reference. The core concept is exposing DOM nodes to the parent component using Angular's ElementRef and ViewChild decorators. You'll work with TypeScript, template references, and event binding to connect the button click to the input focus. By the end, you'll understand how to safely reference and control DOM elements within an Angular application.
intro.usecase: In real applications, forwardRef and DOM node exposure are essential when building reusable form components with complex validation logic. For example, in enterprise dashboards with data tables, you might create a custom filter panel component that needs direct access to specific input fields for focus management or validation state. This pattern also appears in interactive UI libraries where modal dialogs or dropdown menus require programmatic control over their trigger elements. Developers use these techniques to create maintainable component APIs that allow parent components to interact with child DOM elements without breaking encapsulation.
